# Onboard Guide: Space Radiation and Solar Particle Event (SPE) Shelter

## Applies When
- Dosimeter readings exceed 1.0 mGy/day or space weather alert indicates an active Solar Particle Event (SPE) / Coronal Mass Ejection (CME).
- External radiation sensors detect flux exceeding proton threshold energies (>10 MeV, >10 pfu).
- Automated spacecraft alarm announces radiation contingency or mission control issues SPE warning.

## Action Steps
1. Immediately acknowledge and log the alert timestamp, current location in the spacecraft, and personal dosimeter reading.
2. Cease all Extravehicular Activity (EVA) immediately; recall EVA crew back into airlock per standard ingress protocol.
3. Ingress designated storm shelter module (crew quarters or central shielding zone with dense equipment, polyethylene, and water storage walls).
4. Deploy auxiliary water-wall bags and stowage containers around the interior perimeter to maximize mass shielding thickness.
5. Power down non-essential avionics in unshielded compartments to mitigate radiation-induced single-event upsets (SEU).
6. Verify personal active and passive dosimeter badges are worn properly on the chest at all times.
7. Maintain low metabolic activity while sheltered to reduce oxygen consumption and respiratory CO₂ output.

## Escalation Criteria
- Cumulative dosimeter rate exceeds 5.0 mGy/day or prompt alarm indicates extreme SPE.
- Crew member develops nausea, vomiting, sudden profound fatigue, or skin erythema (signs of acute radiation syndrome).
- Primary communications with mission control ground station are lost during high proton flux.
- Contact flight surgeon and Ground Radiation Safety Officer immediately; initiate level 2 radiation emergency checklist.
